title: Deformations of an affine isolated singularity and its completions
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $P$ be a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra, and let $\mathfrak m_1,\ldots,\mathfrak m_r$ be distinct maximal ideals. Assume $V=\operatorname{Spec}P$ is smooth over $k$ outside these points [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $\widehat P_i=\varprojlim_n P_{\mathfrak m_i}/\mathfrak m_i^nP_{\mathfrak m_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Work over Artinian local $k$-algebras with residue field $k$, meaning local rings with the descending chain condition on ideals and with a specified residue-field identification; maps are local $k$-homomorphisms respecting it. A marked deformation of a ring $B$ over $R$ is a flat $R$-algebra $Q$ with an identified quotient $Q/\mathfrak m_RQ\cong B$, and arrows are isomorphisms respecting this quotient [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For $B=P$ the algebras are of finite type over $R$; for $B=\widehat P_i$ they are complete Noetherian local algebras and arrows are continuous. Taking the completed local rings defines a functor from deformations of $P$ to the product of deformations of the $\widehat P_i$. This functor is smooth: for every surjection $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$, every deformation $Q/R$, and every collection of deformations $D_i/R'$ with specified isomorphisms $D_i\otimes_{R'}R\cong\widehat{Q_{\mathfrak m_i}}$, there is a deformation $Q'/R'$ together with isomorphisms $Q'\otimes_{R'}R\cong Q$ and $\widehat{Q'_{\mathfrak m_i}}\cong D_i$ inducing all the specified isomorphisms. On tangent spaces, namely the isomorphism classes over $k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with their deformation vector-space operations, it induces an isomorphism. The empty set of maximal ideals is permitted.

source.place: Tag 0DZF (lemma-isolated), composite to the completed local rings, including tangent-space isomorphism. Complete local deformations and continuous arrows are obtained by completion in Tag 0DYV (lemma-completion); Tag 0DZ5 (lemma-smooth-completion) supplies the smooth comparison.

proof.text: Put $J=\bigcap_i\mathfrak m_i$ (put $J=P$ if $r=0$), and write $\widehat P_J$ for its completion. The field $k$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and $k$; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] therefore makes $P$ Noetherian. Every Artinian coefficient ring is Noetherian with nilpotent maximal ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent]. Thus the inverse image $\mathfrak q_i$ of $\mathfrak m_i$ in any deformation $Q$ is a maximal ideal, and reduction gives a bijection on prime ideals: every prime contains the nilpotent ideal $\mathfrak m_AQ$. The notation $Q_{\mathfrak m_i}$ in the item means $Q_{\mathfrak q_i}$. Apply [lem-sfb-adic-completion-flat-deformation-functor] to $P,J$. We obtain the base-change-compatible functor $F:\mathrm{Def}_P\to\mathrm{Def}_{\widehat P_J}$, $Q\mapsto\widehat Q_{J_Q}$. The source $\mathrm{Def}_P$ may be taken to contain all flat marked deformations: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent] makes every one finite type from its special fibre $P$.

Distinct maximal ideals are comaximal. Their powers are comaximal too: if $a+b=1$, the expansion of $(a+b)^{2n-1}$ lies in $(a^n,b^n)$. For a finite pairwise comaximal family, intersection equals product (for two ideals use $x=x(a+b)$); hence $J^n=\bigcap_i\mathfrak m_i^n$. Apply [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] at each $n\geq1$. The quotient $P/\mathfrak m_i^n$ is already local at $\mathfrak m_i$: every element outside that maximal ideal has an inverse modulo $\mathfrak m_i$, and the remaining nilpotent error is inverted by a finite geometric series. Thus $P/\mathfrak m_i^n\cong P_{\mathfrak m_i}/\mathfrak m_i^nP_{\mathfrak m_i}$. Taking compatible sequences, the coordinate maps and their inverse CRT maps give
$$\widehat P_J\cong\prod_i\widehat P_i.$$
The same calculation for the inverse-image maximal ideals $\mathfrak q_i\subset Q$ identifies $\widehat Q_{J_Q}$ with $\prod_i\widehat{Q_{\mathfrak q_i}}$, naturally in marked isomorphisms and base change.

source.place: Tag 0DZF (lemma-isolated), identity P-completion = product of completed local rings.

proof.text: For any deformation $D$ of $\prod_i\widehat P_i$, its reduction kernel $\mathfrak m_AD$ is nilpotent. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotents-locally-nilpotent], its coordinate idempotents lift uniquely to $e_i\in D$. They are orthogonal because $e_ie_j$ is an idempotent lifting zero, and their sum is one because their orthogonal sum is an idempotent lifting one. Consequently $d\mapsto(e_id)_i$ is an isomorphism $D\cong\prod_i e_iD$, inverse $(d_i)\mapsto\sum_i d_i$. The factors $\widehat P_i$ of $\widehat P_J$ are Noetherian and complete for their maximal ideals: the complete ideal $J\widehat P_J$ projects to $\mathfrak m_i\widehat P_i$, and compatible sequences in a product are coordinatewise. Each factor $e_iD$ is flat since tensor with a direct summand preserves injections, and its special fibre is $\widehat P_i$. By the automatic-completeness assertion of [lem-sfb-adic-completion-flat-deformation-functor], these factors are complete Noetherian local rings. Conversely a finite product of such factors is flat (tensor distributes over finite direct sums). Uniqueness of the lifted idempotents forces arrows and base changes to preserve the factors. This gives an equivalence $\mathrm{Def}_{\widehat P_J}\simeq\prod_i\mathrm{Def}_{\widehat P_i}$, identifying the composite with the completed-local-ring functor in the item. Local ring isomorphisms preserve all powers of maximal ideals, so its arrows are continuous.

The nonsmooth locus is contained in $V(J)=\{\mathfrak m_i\}$. In [lem-sfb-exal-completion-smooth-complement] take $B=P$ and $N=P$, which is finite over itself, to obtain the $k$-linear isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Exal}_k(P,P)\cong\operatorname{Exal}_k(\widehat P_J,\widehat P_J).$$
By [lem-sfb-ring-deformation-smoothness-test] these are precisely the deformation tangent spaces. Its identification sends a dual-number deformation to $0\to P\xrightarrow{\epsilon}Q\to P\to0$; completing that extension is exactly $F(Q)$. Thus this is the tangent map of $F$, not just an abstract vector-space isomorphism. The factor equivalence of step 3 identifies the target tangent space with the product of the local tangent spaces, with coordinatewise operations.

Fix a small extension $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $Q\in\mathrm{Def}_P(A)$. The algebra $Q$ is finite type by the definition of the source deformation groupoid. If $F(Q)$ has a marked flat lift, [lem-sfb-completion-reflects-flat-liftability], applied to $P,J,Q,A',A$, gives a marked flat lift of $Q$. Its hypotheses are exactly finite type of $P$, smoothness off $V(J)$, flatness of $Q$, and the Artinian augmented bases. Step 4 gives tangent surjectivity. Therefore [lem-sfb-ring-deformation-smoothness-test] makes $F$ smooth for every surjection, with the specified reduction isomorphisms. Given the $D_i$ of the item, take $D=\prod_iD_i$ and the product of the specified reduction isomorphisms, using steps 2–3. The criterion gives $Q'$, its reduction marking to $Q$, and a marked isomorphism $F(Q')\cong D$. Coordinate projection gives exactly $\widehat{Q'_{\mathfrak q_i}}\cong D_i$ with the required reduction equations. Although the criterion permits arbitrary flat lifts, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-lift-nilpotent] makes $Q'$ finite type over $A'$ since its quotient $Q$ is finite type and the base kernel is nilpotent.

source.place: Tag 0DZ5 (lemma-smooth-completion), proof using Tag 0DZ3 (lemma-lift-equivalence) and formal-defos.tex Tag 0DYP (lemma-easy-check-smooth).

proof.text: If $r=0$, then $J=P$, the $J$-adic completion is the zero ring, and the product groupoid is terminal. A deformation of the zero algebra satisfies $D=\mathfrak m_AD$; iteration and nilpotence give $D=0$. The preceding argument applies unchanged: its smooth-complement hypothesis says precisely that $P/k$ is smooth everywhere, and the Exal comparison says its tangent space is zero. Thus arbitrary source deformations lift and the map to the zero tangent space is an isomorphism. For $P=0$ all deformation groupoids are terminal by the same iteration. No hypothesis that a listed point is actually singular or that its residue field equals $k$ was used.

source.place: Tag 0DZF (lemma-isolated), empty list and zero-algebra edge cases of the preceding completion argument.
